First convert the quoted energy to a wavelength to see what transition it probably is.

E = 3.9 × 10-6 eV  
 = 3.9 × 10-6 × 1.602 × 10-19 J  
 ≈ 6.25 × 10-25 J

Frequency: ν = E/h ≈ (6.25 × 10-25 J)/(6.626 × 10-34 J s) ≈ 9.4 × 10^8 Hz  
Wavelength: λ = c/ν ≈ (3.0 × 10^8 m s-1)/(9.4 × 10^8 Hz) ≈ 0.32 m ≈ 32 cm

A 32 cm line is the 21 cm (0.21 m) hyper-fine spin-flip line of neutral hydrogen red-shifted by a factor (1+z) ≈ 32/21 ≈ 1.5, corresponding to the ∼2 Gpc distance quoted. Therefore the rest-frame transition is unmistakably the H I 21-cm line.

The 21-cm line is produced by neutral (atomic) hydrogen. In the Milky Way it shows up most prominently in absorption when that hydrogen is cold; in the warm neutral medium the spin temperature is high and the optical depth is too low for strong absorption.

Hence the absorption line is expected from the cold atomic interstellar medium.

Answer: C
